findings.explanation: config.maintenance_window is entirely absent (confirmed against the google provider's actual schema: the block is optional, but start_time/end_time/recurrence are all required once used). Without it, GCP can apply environment maintenance and version updates at any time, including business hours, restarting the scheduler and web server with no predictable window for on-call teams to plan around.
findings.title: Composer environment has no maintenance_window configured

findings.explanation: config.software_config is absent entirely. Confirmed against the google provider schema: image_version is optional and computed, meaning when it's unset GCP selects whatever its current default Composer/Airflow image is at creation time. Two applies of this same module at different points in time (e.g. a dev environment created months after prod) can silently land on different Airflow major/minor versions, producing DAG compatibility drift between environments built from identical Terraform.
findings.remediation: Add a software_config block with an explicit image_version to config, e.g. software_config { image_version = "composer-2-airflow-2" }, ideally exposed as a module variable so callers can choose/upgrade deliberately.
findings.title: Composer environment doesn't pin software_config.image_version

suggested_policies.rationale: coverage_by_type for google_composer_environment (HLD_GCP_100/158/159/374/375/376/485/486) has nothing on maintenance_window. Missing maintenance windows causing unexpected downtime is explicitly a named reliability best-practice pattern, statically detectable (not_null on config.maintenance_window), and applies to any Terraform using google_composer_environment, not just this repo. Validated with `holden validate-policy` (OK).
suggested_policies.yaml:
id: HLD_PROPOSED_BP_001
name: Cloud Composer environments should define a maintenance window
principle: reliability
severity: MEDIUM
rationale: |
  Without config.maintenance_window, Cloud Composer can apply environment
  maintenance and version updates at any time, including business hours,
  causing scheduler/web server restarts and brief DAG-processing
  interruptions with no predictable window for on-call teams to expect them.
remediation: |
  ```hcl
  resource "google_composer_environment" "main" {
    config {
      maintenance_window {
        start_time = "2025-01-05T01:00:00Z"
        end_time   = "2025-01-05T05:00:00Z"
        recurrence = "FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=SA"
      }
    }
  }
  ```
resources:
  google_composer_environment:
    path: config.maintenance_window
    not_null: true

suggested_policies.rationale: coverage_by_type for google_composer_environment has nothing on software_config.image_version. Confirmed via `terraform providers schema -json` that image_version is optional+computed, so its absence is a real non-determinism risk, not a safe provider default being relied on deliberately. Statically detectable (not_null on config.software_config.image_version), applies to any Terraform using google_composer_environment. Validated with `holden validate-policy` (OK).
suggested_policies.yaml:
id: HLD_PROPOSED_BP_002
name: Cloud Composer environments should pin software_config.image_version
principle: repeatability
severity: LOW
rationale: |
  image_version is optional and computed in the provider schema — when
  config.software_config (or image_version within it) is omitted, GCP
  selects its current default Composer/Airflow image at creation time.
  Two applies of the same Terraform at different points in time can then
  provision meaningfully different Airflow versions, producing DAG
  compatibility drift between environments that should be identical.
remediation: |
  ```hcl
  resource "google_composer_environment" "main" {
    config {
      software_config {
        image_version = "composer-2-airflow-2"
      }
    }
  }
  ```
resources:
  google_composer_environment:
    path: config.software_config.image_version
    not_null: true
